NRL Casualty Ward: Walsh, Metcalf injury drama; Trindall dislocates shoulder
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh and Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf may have played their last match of the season after being forced from the field with injuries in Saturday night's match at Suncorp Stadium.
Walsh's World Cup hopes are in doubt after the Kangaroos fullback suffered a syndesmosis injury midway through the first half and Metcalf followed him up the tunnel soon after with another hamstring injury.
The drama occurred within minutes of each other, with Warriors fullback Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad sinbinned for a hip drop tackle on Walsh, who shrugged off a Broncos trainer and insisted he wanted to play on.
From the penalty, Walsh injected himself into the play and threw an intercept pass for Warriors winger Alofiana Khan-Pereira to race away and score.
Walsh hobbled from the field and up the tunnel. He was sent for scans and may have played his last game for the Broncos this season.
Metcalf, who returned last week from a four month lay off with a hamstring injury, missed the conversion and immediately clutched at the back of his right leg.
He came from the field and Warriors medical staff immediately strapped ice to his the back of his thigh.
Warriors coach Andrew Webster said: "Luke's got a hamstring history, but to do it kicking the goal is the first time that's ever happened to him and he's obviously gutted. But look, we're always optimistic and hopefully we can get him back in time and he can play a part in the back end of the season".
Metcalf leaves the field
Cronulla playmaker Braydon Trindall was forced from the field after dislocating his shoulder at Ocean Protect Stadium on Saturday.
Trindall had just got his side's first try in the opening moments of the match, but landed awkwardly, coming from the field immediately after scoring.
Medical staff were able to get it back in, but the call was made to sit him out and await further scans.
Trindall dislocates shoulder while scoring try
The Sharks came into the game without Jesse Ramien , who has played his final game for the club with the centre undergoing season-ending pectoral surgery on Thursday.
Ramien suffered the injury in the second half of last week's loss to St George Illawarra and will depart the Sharks at the end of the season to join the Cowboys.
The Raiders too were stuck an injury blow in the match, with English forward Morgan Smithies failing his HIA in the first half.
Broncos veteran Adam Reynolds faces a battle to return to the field before hanging up the boots after suffering a calf strain at training on Wednesday.
The premiership winner has not played since suffering a head knock in the Round 22 loss to the Knights and the latest setback puts his hopes of playing out his final season before retiring at the end of the year at risk.
In a statement, the Broncos said Reynolds will be assessed on a weekly basis to determine a return to play.

Gold Coast , meanwhile, were poor last weekend and will continue to struggle without the organising influence they had received from young halfback Zane Harrison.
The current spread of Knights -13.5 is large, but I am happy to lay it. Newcastle already belted Gold Coast 36-12 during Magic Round earlier this season, and their attacking lineup now looks close to full strength. The Knights have won 12 games and remain in the top six, while the Titans sit near the bottom and have little beyond pride to play for.

The Titans then equalled a club record with their fifth-straight victory as they toppled the Sharks 24-10 at Ocean Protect Stadium.

Late mail: Ieremia ruled out, De Groot to start in Newcastle
Jaylan De Groot will start on the wing against the team he debuted against two years ago, replacing Dean Ieremia who has been ruled out of the Titans' Knights clash with a hamstring injury.
The 23-year-old remains part of the back five in his eighth NRL appearance of the season after playing left centre last week - AJ Brimson returning to that role with Lachlan Ilias to come into the halves for the first time since Round 9.
The remainder of Josh Hannay's team remains unchanged with Siale Faeamani elevated to the six-man bench to cover De Groot's promotion - his side eyeing back-to-back wins at McDonald Jones Stadium after defeating the Knights in the corresponding fixture last season.

In week two of Indigenous Round, the Titans will again wear a specially-designed jersey by local artist Christine Slabb, showcasing the club's connection to country, community, culture and each other.

Tigers vs Dragons Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 24 2026
August 15 th 2026, 12:34am , By: Ben Bridge
And now, for anyone who has survived the first seven games of NRL Round 24 , we arrive at this monstrosity.
Sunday afternoon at CommBank Stadium gives us the Tigers against the Dragons , a matchup between 14th and 17th where neither team has earned anything resembling betting trust. The Dragons are coming off their best victory of the season, upsetting bitter rivals Cronulla 24-16 at Kogarah. Wests had the bye last week, which at least meant they managed to get through an entire weekend without appearing in another crisis headline.
Disgustingly, I am taking the Tigers to win.
The logic is largely situational. St George Illawarra poured everything into last week’s local derby, producing enormous defensive efforts from Jacob Liddle, Ryan Couchman and Clint Gutherson. It was their Grand Final. Reproducing that emotional level seven days later against another bottom 4 side at CommBank Stadium is a completely different challenge.
Wests have lost seven straight and been outscored 208-67 across that stretch, so there is absolutely no pretending this is a high confidence selection. But they finally enjoyed a quieter week, have Jarome Luai, Adam Doueihi, Api Koroisau, Jahream Bula and their key forwards available, and might have one last decent performance left in them.
Hold your nose.
Tigers vs Dragons Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 24
Tigers Finally Get a Week Away From the Circus
Wests’ most recent game was the 16-13 loss to Parramatta in Round 22, before their Round 23 bye. It was hardly inspiring football. The Eels completed just 67 per cent, made 19 errors and handed the Tigers repeated opportunities to win, yet Wests still found a way to lose. Adam Doueihi briefly put them ahead with a field goal before Parramatta stole the result late.
The positive is that it was at least competitive. After some truly horrendous defensive performances across the previous month, the Tigers restricted Parramatta to 16 and remained in the game for the full 80 minutes.
The bye may have been exactly what this club needed.
There has been relentless scrutiny around Benji Marshall and the playing group, and the Tigers have looked emotionally exhausted as much as physically poor. Having a weekend where they were not required to play, and, importantly, were not the centre of another match day disaster, could allow them to reset.
The team list contains genuine talent. Bula remains dangerous from fullback, Luai and Doueihi form an experienced halves pairing and Koroisau is still capable of controlling a match from dummy half. Terrell May and Fonua Pole give them power through the middle, with Samuela Fainu, Alex Twal, Sione Fainu and Bunty Afoa adding plenty of size.
The backline has been reshuffled again. NSW Cup leading try scorer Solomone Saukuru is set for his NRL debut in the centres, while Junior Tupou and Sunia Turuva occupy the wings. Heamasi Makasini and Starford To’a are out.
There are absolutely no guarantees. But after seven straight defeats, the Tigers are at least rested and facing the only team around their level in my power ratings.
Dragons Produce Their Grand Final Performance
St George Illawarra’s 24-16 upset of Cronulla was easily their best win of the season. The Dragons entered as huge underdogs against a Sharks side sitting fourth but defended with enormous commitment and found the decisive attacking moments late. Setu Tu scored in the 77th minute to seal the result after Cronulla had briefly levelled the scores at 16-16.
